summary.text: Salud Carbajal is the Democratic incumbent for California's 24th District. Born in Mexico and raised in California, he is a Marine Corps Reserve veteran who served on the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors for 12 years before his first election to Congress in 2016. He sits on the Armed Services, Agriculture, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Carbajal emigrated from Mexico to the United States at age 5 and worked summers as a farmworker with his father, according to his House biography. He was the first in his family to graduate from a university, earning a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Santa Barbara, in 1990, and later earned a master's degree in organizational management from Fielding Graduate University in 1994.
He served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve from 1984 to 1992, and his House biography says he was mobilized to active duty during the 1992 Gulf War.

From 1993 to 2004 Carbajal worked on the staff of Santa Barbara County Supervisor Naomi Schwartz, and he also worked in the county Public Health Department. He then served on the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors from 2004 to 2016.

Carbajal was elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and first took office in 2017. In the 2025-2026 Congress he serves on the Armed Services, Agriculture, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, and he is ranking member of the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee.

His House biography says multiple bills he sponsored were signed into law, including bills responding to the 2019 Conception boat fire and promoting 'red flag' laws, and that he helped write the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law as a member of Transportation and Infrastructure. He is married to Gina, and they have two children, Natasha and Michael, according to the biography.
